coverage_gaps: Alias imports are handled only where observed: utils/_os.py (from os.path import abspath, dirname, join, normcase), core/management/templates.py (from os import path), core/files/move.py (from shutil import copystat). Other modules that re-export os.path members (if any appear) would be missed by the qualified-form match.

pathlib attribute reads that are not calls are not extracted: pathlib.PurePath(dir_name).parts traversal checks (storage.py:71, storage.py:106, db path checks) - .parts is an attribute, not a call; recorded here as sanitizer evidence instead of candidate rows.

pathlib .is_dir()/.exists()/.stat()/.is_file() attribute-name calls are only extracted for views/static.py and contrib/admindocs/views.py (the request-path-driven sites); a package-wide match would collide with QuerySet.exists() and other same-named methods.

Path-method family (Attribute-name matching for .open/.read_text/.write_text/.read_bytes/.write_bytes/.iterdir) cannot constrain the receiver to a pathlib Path at AST level; non-Path .open receivers (self.storage.open, self.file.open) also match and are additionally covered by the dedicated storage-wrapper family - the same call node can therefore yield two rows with different flow_kind (same policy as the api/ast duplicate rows of the prior projects).
os.environ.get is extracted package-wide via API graphs plus the qualified syntax shape; bare-name `from os import environ` aliases were not observed in the package.

Dynamic dispatch: no copyparty-style dynamic open (open_func = open) was observed in the audited paths; getattr-based attribute dispatch (e.g. FileProxyMixin property forwarding, FileResponse filelike.read) is not call-site matched.

urlretrieve (urllib.request, core/management/templates.py:259) downloads the --template URL to a temp file; it is a network-fetch boundary (Pass 3 shape), emitted only via the CLI source rows and the archive/open sink rows around it, not as its own sink family.

tempfile.mkdtemp/mkstemp/NamedTemporaryFile destinations are internal temp directories; the only attacker-influenced fragment is the NamedTemporaryFile suffix derived from os.path.splitext of the upload name (uploadedfile.py:63-:64), which cannot contain path separators after splitext - no sink family emitted for tempfile.

request.headers (http/request.py:70-:72) is a cached_property over META; header values surface as request.META['HTTP_*'] reads - covered by the request.META attribute family rather than a separate headers family.
